newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-THIRD TEST WIN JUST AS IMPORTANT-MCGEECHAN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-THIRD TEST WIN JUST AS IMPORTANT-MCGEECHAN.

text.p: British Lions coach Ian McGeechan said winning next Saturday's third test for a series cleansweep would be as important as his side's first two victories over South Africa.

"Winning the third test in Johannesburg this Saturday is just as important," McGeechan said after steering his side to a series clinching 18-15 victory over the Springboks in the second test at King's Park at the weekend.
"And the players themselves want to continue in the same vein. The spirit on this tour has been fantastic and you can't ask for anything more than that."
The Lions meet Northern Free State in Welkom on Tuesday before their final match, the third test at Ellis Park on Saturday.
McGeechan said it was unlikely that fringe test players in the squad, who had performed well in the mid-week games, would be rewarded with selection for the final clash against the world champions.

"What we want to do is put our best combinations out again and ensure that we have the right balance -- balance in the back row, balance in the midfield, balance in the front row and balance in the back three," he said.
McGeechan said a particular area of delicate balance was in the Lions midfield where Welsh centre Scott Gibbs had played a vital role.

"We didn't get all the midfield combinations we wanted on this tour because of injuries and Scott's role at centre has been significant -- he is a player who has really thrived in the Lions environment.

"The midfield is where you sometimes need a balance of strength, guile and pace. Scott's hands are as important as his strength but then we've got different styled players like Jeremy Guscott and Gregor Townsend outside him -- and those players are able to work in other areas as well to help the balance."
